context:
Goal: one clear verdict for each way an agent can run a bigger model than its role allows.
Problem (rule): today a two-step jump to Opus only asks while a one-step jump to Sonnet is refused for good, so the costliest jump gets the softest check, and each case needs your verdict.
Based on (code): the guard refuses a Haiku role on Sonnet with no override and skips Opus; a separate check only asks for Opus (the lane's read of main, Nov 1).
Departs from: main (Haiku role on Sonnet refused for good; any role on Opus asks) — the verdicts you pick.

Three cases: (1) a Haiku role on Sonnet, one step up; (2) a Sonnet role on Opus, one step up; (3) a Haiku role on Opus, two steps up. Four verdicts fit each: allow, ask you, refuse with your typed override as the way out, or refuse with no way out. In every option a marker (Round N of 3, or Audit:) or a standing grant still lets an agent through. To set each case on its own, pick None of these and write the three verdicts in your note.

lastAnswer.note: A is fine -- but separately, I thought we've covered all the ways a session/agent can pick the wrong model -- so is this moot? and if we haven't covered all the ways, how /why?

options.gain: One rule, no softer path for Opus, and you keep a way out.
options.how: Every case is refused; you type override to let one through.
options.label: All three: refuse, your override lifts it
options.lose: Opus agents that only asked today stop until you type override.

options.how: Every case stops and asks you.
options.label: All three: ask you
options.lose: Case 1, refused today, runs on one yes.

options.how: Every case is refused, with no override.
options.label: All three: refuse, nothing lifts it
options.lose: No way past, even for you.

options.gain: The biggest jump is the strictest.
options.how: One step up (cases 1 and 2): refuse, your override lifts it. Two steps up (case 3): refuse, nothing lifts it.
options.label: By distance, strict

options.how: One step up asks you; two steps up is refused, your override lifts it.
options.label: By distance, softer
options.lose: More questions, and case 1 is softer than today.

options.how: Up to Sonnet (case 1) asks you; up to Opus (cases 2 and 3) is refused, your override lifts it.
options.label: By model

options.how: Case 1 refused for good; cases 2 and 3 ask.
options.label: Keep today
options.lose: The costliest jump keeps the softest check.

reply: Filed as a: a model above the role's is refused, and your typed override lifts it. Your question is answered on item 137.
title: When an agent runs a bigger model than its role allows, what happens in each case?
why: One rule for every case, with no softer path for the costliest model, and your override keeps the rare yes.
